cards.text: Jeremiah, the prophet, has warned the people of Judah again and again for twenty-three years, and they have not listened (Jeremiah 25:3). That's hitting snooze on the same alarm for twenty-three YEARS. Now the prophet tells us what the LORD, the God of Israel, said to him next.

cards.question: The LORD tells Jeremiah to take something from His hand. What is it?

cards.text: It's the cup of the wine of wrath, and the LORD wants Jeremiah to pass it around (Jeremiah 25:15). I was nervous about baking COOKIES for the Most High, and Jeremiah gets handed THIS job?

cards.question: Jeremiah has to make all the ___ the LORD sends him to drink from the cup of the wine of wrath.

cards.text: Then the LORD says what happens once they drink. They stagger and go out of their minds (Jeremiah 25:16).

cards.question: The LORD says the nations will stagger and go out of their minds because of a famine He will send among them.
When the LORD hands Jeremiah the cup of the wine of wrath, Jeremiah refuses to take it.

cards.text: So Jeremiah takes the cup and makes every nation the LORD sent him to drink from it, to make them a ruin. It's a long list of kings and nations, and first in line are Jerusalem and the cities of Judah (Jeremiah 25:17-26).
Then Jeremiah is to tell them what the LORD of Hosts says: “Drink, get drunk, and vomit. Fall down and never get up again, because of the sword I will send among you.” (Jeremiah 25:27)
But what if a nation won't take the cup? Friend, if that cup came my way, I'd be hopping backward on this gold base so fast my chef's hat would fly off.

cards.question: What does the LORD tell Jeremiah to say if a nation refuses to take the cup and drink it?

cards.text: Then the LORD gives the reason. He is beginning to bring disaster on the city that bears His Name (Jeremiah 25:29).

cards.question: Since the LORD is starting with the city that bears His Name, He says the other nations can go unpunished.
The LORD of Hosts says He is calling down a sword. On whom?

answers.text: All the inhabitants of the earth
All the beasts of the field
All the idols of the nations

cards.text: Now the message turns from a cup to a sound, coming from on high, from the LORD's holy habitation (Jeremiah 25:30). Friend, I'm putting the dough down for this one.

cards.question: Jeremiah says the LORD will make a sound from on high over His pasture. What kind of sound?

cards.text: Like those who tread the grapes, He will call out with a shout against all the inhabitants of the earth (Jeremiah 25:30).

cards.question: Jeremiah says the tumult will resound to the ends of the earth. Why?

answers.text: The LORD brings a charge against the nations
The nations go to war with each other
The sea rises up over the land

cards.question: In this message, the LORD's judgment falls only on the people of Judah.

cards.text: Then the LORD of Hosts says disaster is spreading from nation to nation (Jeremiah 25:32). And it's coming from far off, the kind of thing you can see building on the horizon.

cards.question: The LORD of Hosts says a mighty ___ is rising from the ends of the earth.

cards.text: Then the prophet says those slain by the LORD on that day will be spread from one end of the earth to the other (Jeremiah 25:33).

cards.question: Jeremiah says the people slain by the LORD on that day will be mourned and buried.

cards.text: Now Jeremiah turns to the shepherds, the leaders of the flock. The days of their slaughter have come (Jeremiah 25:34).

cards.question: The days of slaughter have come for the shepherds. What does Jeremiah tell them to do?
When disaster comes, the shepherds and the leaders of the flock will find a way to escape.

cards.text: They'll fall and be shattered like fine pottery, and escape will elude them (Jeremiah 25:34-35). Friend, I can't even sneak away from a burnt batch in my own bakery. The smoke alarm finds me EVERY time.
Then Jeremiah says to listen: you can hear the cry of the shepherds, the wailing of the leaders of the flock (Jeremiah 25:36).

cards.question: The shepherds are wailing because the LORD is destroying their ___.

cards.text: The peaceful meadows have been silenced because of the LORD's burning anger (Jeremiah 25:37). After all that wailing, it goes quiet.

cards.question: Remember the LORD roaring from on high? In the last line, Jeremiah says He has left His den like a ___.

cards.text: Their land has been made a desolation by the sword of the oppressor, and because of the fierce anger of the LORD (Jeremiah 25:38). Heavy word, friend, and you walked through every line of it with me.

findings.problem: The card says Jeremiah 'has warned' the people for twenty-three years, citing Jeremiah 25:3. Jeremiah 25:3 says the word of the LORD came to Jeremiah and he has 'spoken to you again and again.' It doesn't call it warning.

rule.text: Call things what the text calls them.

findings.problem: Card 8 already says Jeremiah makes every nation the LORD sent him to drink from the cup 'to make them a ruin,' and that it's a long list of kings and nations. That gives away the answer to this true or false question about whether the other nations can go unpunished.

rule.text: No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later.

findings.problem: Story card 3, just before this card, says He will call out 'against all the inhabitants of the earth.' Stop 1 card 14's answer is also 'All the inhabitants of the earth.' Both give away the answer to this true or false question about whether judgment falls only on Judah.

rule.text: No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later.

findings.problem: This story card has 3 sentences. Only the opening card can have up to 3.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: Card 12 already asked about Jeremiah 25:35 and answered it. This card repeats 'escape will elude them' from that verse, then goes back to the pottery detail from Jeremiah 25:34. It recaps instead of moving forward. The pottery detail belongs with card 10, which tells verse 34.

rule.text: Every story card moves the baker forward through the passage. No recap cards.
